messages.subject: On the meaning of the parameters of the output of the dd_hyperbolic function
messages.subject_clean: On the meaning of the parameters of the output of the dd_hyperbolic function
messages.body_plain:
Dear developers and users of hbayesDM

I would like to ask about the meaning of the output parameters of the dd_hyperbolic function.

Is it correct that the group level parameter "mu_k" is output, and the "sd" in this case simply means the sd of "mu_k"?

If so, what does the additional "sigma[1]" mean?
Also, what does the "sd" in "sigma[1]" mean in addition?

I would appreciate your answer.

ーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
小牧 和哉
大阪大学大学院　人間科学研究科　博士前期課程2回生
KOMAKI Kazuya, second-year graduate student,
Graduate School of Human Sciences, Osaka University, Japan.

messages.subject: CGT_CM Application in Repeated Measures Design?
messages.subject_clean: CGT_CM Application in Repeated Measures Design?
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am new to Bayesian statistics and have been using hBayesDM to model trial-by-trial data from the Cambridge Gambling Task. We are interested in seeing whether individuals undergoing treatment for a substance use disorder show any changes in their performance on the CGT post-treatment and whether they differ significantly from controls.

We are looking for clarification about whether the hBayesDM (specifically, cgt_cm) is appropriate for comparing their performance pre- and post-treatment?

Thank you!

Kind regards,
Laura
